listSrc: Maine Department of the Secretary of State

items.t: Lowered Maine's top marginal income tax rate from 8.5 percent to 7.15 percent as governor.
items.q: The governor lowered the top marginal tax rate from 8.5 percent to 7.15 percent, the largest tax cut in Maine's history.

items.t: Prioritized lowering taxes, lowering energy costs, and cutting regulations as governor.
items.q: Governor LePage has prioritized lowering taxes, lowering energy costs, and cutting regulations.

items.t: As Waterville mayor, worked across party lines to reduce taxes each year and increase the city's rainy day fund.
items.q: the Governor worked across party lines to reduce taxes each year, improve the City's credit rating, increase the rainy day fund and maintain strong support for local education

items.t: Reduced the size of state government while saying essential services were not cut.
items.q: Governor LePage has shrunk the size of state government without cutting essential services.

items.t: Rebuilt Maine's budget stabilization fund, known as the rainy day fund.
items.q: He has rebuilt the state's budget stabilization fund

items.t: His administration eliminated a $1.7 billion shortfall in the state pension system while protecting retirees' future benefits.
items.q: His administration eliminated a $1.7 billion shortfall in Maine's government pension system while protecting retiree's future benefits.

items.t: Used the state's liquor revenue to pay off Maine's debt to hospitals.
items.q: The Governor found a way to use the state's liquor revenue to pay off the hospitals

items.t: Worked on the Medicaid budget shortfall and on reforming Maine's welfare system as governor.
items.q: One of the areas where he has had the greatest successes has been in solving the budget crisis created by the expansion of Medicaid in 2002 and reforming Maine's welfare system.

items.t: Increased funding for nursing facilities, homecare support, and services for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
items.q: increasing funding for nursing facilities by over 40 percent since 2011, financial support for homecare by over 60 percent, and providing an additional $100 million since 2011 for those with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

items.t: Exempted military retiree pension income from the Maine state income tax as governor.
items.q: He also exempted Military retiree pension income from the state income tax.
